comparator.name: Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology
comparator.sourceNotes: The official current study-programme page publishes a complete 180-ECTS curriculum: a 60-ECTS first-year anthropology foundation, a 60-ECTS second year combining theory, global debates, ethnographic research and restricted choice, and a 60-ECTS third year with professional development, anthropology theme courses and free choice. Published choice aggregates are preserved without inventing specific annual or individual selections.
components: Two exploration courses selected from the published anthropology options.
One regional course; annual offerings may vary.
Two anthropology theme courses selected from the published specialisation space.
Genuine elective space; no minor, internship or exchange package is invented.

core: Cultural anthropology, development sociology, identity and global social change
Ethnographic and qualitative research through observation, interviewing, interpretation and writing
Anthropological theory, history, comparison and regional knowledge
adjacent: Power, politics, geopolitics, inequality and migration
Ecology, climate change and relationships between culture and environment
Media, visual culture, data and technology in changing societies
Body, health, medicine, organisations and applied anthropology
questions: How do people create cultural meaning, identity and difference in everyday life?
How do power, inequality, migration and geopolitics reshape communities?
How do climate change, ecology, media and technology transform social relationships?

candidates.label: Power, Politics & Geopolitical Anthropology
candidates.reason: Power, inequality, geopolitics and politics already form a substantial part of the closest match rather than a separate remaining programme direction.

candidates.label: Body, Medical & Applied Anthropology
candidates.reason: This is a coherent direction, but three alternatives are already included.

alternatives.label: Anthropology, Culture & Global Change
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum visibly combines culture, society, identity, global change and qualitative inquiry without implying a dedicated ethnographic fieldwork degree.
alternatives.concept: A closest feasible anthropology pathway combining cultural difference, identity, global change, development, power, qualitative research, history, politics, communication and media.
progression: Sociology, history, rhetoric, qualitative research and philosophy foundations precede modern sociology, politics, advanced media, cultural analysis and research seminars. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass, with eight 300-level courses.

alternatives.label: Ecology, Communities & Global Change
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum combines social and cultural analysis with climate, sustainability, ecology and community responses to global change.
alternatives.concept: Builds the evidenced ecology-and-anthropology direction around climate change, sustainability, communities, environmental governance, globalisation, migration and qualitative social research.
progression: Sociology, sustainability, qualitative research and environmental foundations precede political sociology, climate governance, advanced environmental study and research seminars. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass, with eight 300-level courses.
alternatives.distinctness: This route makes ecology, climate and community responses the central anthropological application; it differs from both other programmes by more than four courses and 30 EC.

alternatives.label: Media, Visual Culture & Digital Anthropology
alternatives.concept: Builds the evidenced media, visual and data-and-technology directions around cultural inequality, politics, visual social inquiry, documentary media, digital methods and qualitative research.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines cultural and social theory with film, media, visual inquiry, politics and data analysis; the label states those visible strands directly.
progression: Sociology, history, media and qualitative-research foundations precede politics, advanced visual culture, media analysis and research seminars. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass, with eight 300-level courses.
alternatives.distinctness: This route centres visual media, digital culture and technology as anthropological objects and methods; it differs from both the broad closest match and the ecology route by more than four courses and 30 EC.

blocks: Both introduce systematic study of societies, culture and social relations, although UvA provides the dedicated anthropology foundation.
Both develop qualitative research design, interviewing, observation, analysis and interpretation.
Both use historical inquiry to situate social and cultural concepts and transformations.
Both address advanced contemporary social theory, inequality and changing societies.
Both culminate in advanced research synthesis and presentation of a sustained social-science inquiry.
Both develop close analysis and effective written argumentation about communication and cultural meaning.
Both examine epistemological and normative foundations of studying human societies.
Both support advanced visual and media-based cultural inquiry within a thematic specialisation.
Both allow social and cultural inquiry to be communicated through creative media formats.
Both support reflection on academic development, professional identity and future pathways.
No single selected UCR course is presented as a direct counterpart to Current Debates 1: Connecting Worlds.
No single selected UCR course is presented as a direct counterpart to Practicing Ethnography.
No single selected UCR course is presented as a direct counterpart to Restricted-choice electives: Exploration Courses.
No single selected UCR course is presented as a direct counterpart to Restricted-choice electives: Regional Course.
No single selected UCR course is presented as a direct counterpart to Free-choice elective.
No single selected UCR course is presented as a direct counterpart to Future Perspectives.
No single selected UCR course is presented as a direct counterpart to Free-choice electives.

selection.assessment: The closest match owns the programme-defining cultural-anthropology, development-sociology and ethnographic-research interests. Ecology/global change and media/visual/digital anthropology are the two strongest coherent remaining directions and yield feasible, substantively distinct programmes. Power and politics are already covered by the closest match; body, medical and applied anthropology remains coherent but cannot be added after the maximum of three alternatives is reached.

notes.text: UvA provides a dedicated anthropology curriculum with sequenced theory, ethnographic methods and a separately credited fieldwork project. UCR can assemble a strong cultural and qualitative social-science pathway, but does not reproduce that disciplinary sequence.
UvA publishes exploration, regional, theme and free-choice spaces as credit aggregates. They are retained without inventing annual course offerings or an individual specialisation package.
